mission.title: The Chateau
mission.description: Hear the Merovingian out on the loose interface program, then follow the failures in the white hallways back to the chateau.

npc.say: I do not know how that woman managed to resurrect herself as a polygonal monster, but considering the rest of her history, I do not think we need be overawed by her appearance; she may be clever, but she possesses an interesting flaw: she imagines herself to be acting on a universal scale, and neglects to consider the individual results of her actions.
You can't keep a good program down, we always say.
Get me hall control! Why aren't they responding! Damn it!
Something able to access all those doors could get just about anywhere...
I've found it's best not to comment on their...er...stature.

I'm surprised that Flood's connection to you lasted as long as it did; I tried to contact him before I left the construct, but he did not respond; he must have been entirely unaware of what was happening around him.

phase.briefing:
That obnoxious Wright woman's arrival forced us to jettison the biological interface program into the simulation at large. I imagine it's hanging around helplessly out there somewhere, just waiting to be snatched by the first cherry-picker, be that Wright or--Turing forbid--some gang of Zionites. We won't even think about those Pluribus Neo people.
In any case, the Merovingian has something to say to you about it, so keep your ears open, and your mouth shut.

enter.say: So I guess they're pretty sure that glowing wireframed woman who showed up was Danielle Wright, huh? Funny, wasn't she supposed to have been killed by the Machines for making an improved red pill program after the Truce ended?

talk.say:
Many people would like to get that program, {player}, but they will find themselves disappointed. I allowed it to be released temporarily, but only as a means of foiling my enemy; I mean to get it back, and woe betide the fool who stands in my way.
Now, let us see what we can do, hm? Vite, vite!

near.say: We were dead once, too, and now look at us.

phase.briefing: Some of our people haven't been sleeping on the job, operative, and are already looking into finding that little lost program. You need to go talk to Arago, one of those who's been monitoring the situation, and get yourself caught up with the rest of us.

talk.say: We can't actually detect the program itself, but we can look for signs of--

Get me hall control! Why aren't they responding! Damn it!
Operative! Yes, you! Get over there!

near.say: I've found it's best not to comment on their...er...stature.

phase.briefing:
You heard the little goblin, operative: to the hallway control center with you! Do I have to do all the thinking around here?
Hm... No point in asking that, probably...

enter.say: The white hallways provide handy backdoors for accessing our various constructs and hideaways. You need a specially encoded key to get through any of the doorways--at least, that's how it's supposed to work.

done.say:
Uh-oh. The hallway controls are not responding. This isn't--
Oh, nuts. As if things weren't complicated enough, look who decides to show up.
Uh! Hm... Er... What'd you do?

talk.say: Wooh... I feel a...nap coming on...

phase.briefing:
The hallway control is a shambles, eh? No, I don't blame you; you hardly have the technical know-how to screw something that secure up. The Effectuator, on the other hand...
Mm, there's Malphas pinging in. Must have just got out of the chateau here by the skin of his freakish teeth.
Hmph. As long as our supply of tonics holds out, I won't be too***********

enter.say: Dunno what happened, but I can't get ahold of Flood now. Mixed blessing, I suppose... Maybe Malphas will have some ideas about what's going on with the hallways and chateau.

talk.say:
There has been a series of system failures throughout the chateau. Despite our best efforts, we were not able to detect the source, but it must have been internal, because failures continued in new systems even after we shut down nearly all external connections.
This very inability to detect the source leads me to posit that the source is, in fact, the interface program itself, which Silver's experiments showed could bypass security measures with ease. How it got there I...can't imagine, but possibly it found a connection back to our networks from somewhere close to where it was dumped by the Merovingian.

done.say: That explains why we lost contact with Flood. How'd he not notice all those system failures? He was there the whole time.
